originalAlarm.description: `__curr_1644` could be null (null value originating from line 2678) and is dereferenced.

sanitizedDescription: `curr` could be null (null value originating from line 2678) and is dereferenced.
reasoning: TRUE POSITIVE (NEW, OVER-CONSTRAINED): 2631486f1bf.c (BusyBox ls). '`curr` could be null (null value originating from malloc) and is dereferenced' at line 67 ('curr->next = head'). Same root cause as TRANSFORMATION_94 (null dereference after malloc without NULL check at line 65). 'curr = malloc(sizeof(struct dnode))' can return NULL; 'curr->next = head' at line 67 would then dereference NULL. NEW: the annotated vbdb bug is the uninitialized 'head' pointer, not null-after-malloc. OVER-CONSTRAINED: line 67 is NOT inside any '#ifdef' block — the null dereference exists in ALL configurations regardless of CONFIG_FEATURE_LS_SORTFILES. Requiring CONFIG_FEATURE_LS_SORTFILES=true is too narrow; the correct condition is unconstrained (any config). The sort() call inside '#ifdef CONFIG_FEATURE_LS_SORTFILES' likely causes Pulse to trace a specific execution path that reveals the bug, but the bug itself is config-independent.
